card.name: The word have after who do not
card.fires_on: The word "have" right after "who do not" or "who does not" in a relative clause about a patient group. It marks a contrast with patients who lack a condition, risk factor, or response.

modes.label: Patients who lack a condition
modes.description: "have" follows "patients who do/does not" and is followed by a condition, procedure or risk factor.
modes.example: may trigger an angle-closure attack in a patient with anatomically narrow angles who does not<< have>> a patent iridectomy. Use in

modes.label: Patients lacking a response or disease
modes.description: "have" after "do not" is followed by a response or underlying disease in a label warning.
modes.example: Discontinue fenofibric acid delayed-release capsules in patients who do not<< have>> an adequate response after two months of treatment

card.plain: It lights up on the word "have" in phrases like "patients who do not have" a certain condition.
